passages.scripture: Therefore let us leave the elementary teachings about Christ and go on to maturity, not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith in God, instruction about baptisms, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.

lines.text: We turn away from sinful deeds that lead to death.
We put our faith in God, who gives us eternal life.
We learn about baptisms.
We learn about the laying on of hands.
One day, the dead will be raised back to life.
One day God will judge everyone, and His judgments will last forever.
All these are the basic, foundational teachings about Christ.
We do not need to teach these basic teachings all over again — they are foundational, and everything else we learn about Christ is built on top of them.
So let us move on from these basic lessons, and go on to maturity.

passages.scripture: And this we will do, if God permits.

lines.text: And we will do this — we will go on to maturity.
We can only do this if God permits it.

passages.scripture: It is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, who have shared in the Holy Spirit, who have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the coming age— and then have fallen away—to be restored to repentance, because they themselves are crucifying the Son of God all over again and subjecting Him to open shame.

lines.text: Some people have once been enlightened.
They have tasted the heavenly gift.
They have shared in the Holy Spirit.
They have tasted the goodness of God's word.
And they have tasted the powers of the coming age.
Suppose one of these people falls away.
Then it is impossible to restore such a person to repentance.
This is because, to their own harm, they are crucifying the Son of God all over again.
And they are exposing Christ to open shame.

passages.scripture: For land that drinks in the rain often falling on it and that produces a crop useful to those for whom it is tended receives the blessing of God.

lines.text: For the land drinks in the rain that keeps falling on it — Christians receive from God His word and His Spirit.
The land grows a crop that is good for something — these Christians do good works.
The crop is useful to the people the land is farmed for — these good works help other people.
And God blesses that land — God blesses these Christians.

passages.scripture: But land that produces thorns and thistles is worthless, and its curse is imminent. In the end it will be burned.

lines.text: But the same land can produce thorns and thistles — someone could receive from God His word and His Spirit, but continue disobeying Him.
That land is worthless — disobeying God does not help other people.
That land is near to being cursed — that person is near to God cursing them.
In the end that land is burned — God judges those who received from God, but lived lives of disobedience.

passages.scripture: Even though we speak like this, beloved, we are convinced of better things in your case—things that accompany salvation.

lines.text: We have spoken to you like this — the warning about the burned land was severe.
But you are dearly loved.
And in your case we are sure of better things.
These better things come with salvation — we are sure that your salvation will include obedience to God and His blessings.

passages.scripture: For God is not unjust. He will not forget your work and the love you have shown for His name as you have ministered to the saints and continue to do so.

lines.text: For God is not unjust.
God will not forget your work.
And God will not forget the love you have shown for His name.
You have served the saints — the saints are fellow Christians, set apart for God.
And you keep on serving them.

passages.scripture: We want each of you to show this same diligence to the very end, in order to make your hope sure.

lines.text: We want each of you to show this same diligence serving God's people — diligence is steady work, not a burst of effort that leaves you too tired to continue.
Keep showing this diligence to the very end — diligence means making a little progress all the time, and continually learning to do that a little better.
Do this in order to make your hope sure.
A sure hope means what God has promised you is fully certain.

passages.scripture: Then you will not be sluggish, but will imitate those who through faith and patience inherit what has been promised.

lines.text: God has promised an inheritance.
There are those who inherit what God has promised.
Those who inherit what God has promised inherit it through faith.
Those who inherit what God has promised inherit it through patience — patience means waiting a long time for God, never giving up.
If you are diligent until the end, then you will not be sluggish — sluggish means slow to move, dragging your feet.
Instead of being sluggish, you will imitate those who inherit — to imitate them is to copy the way they live.

passages.scripture: When God made His promise to Abraham, since He had no one greater to swear by, He swore by Himself, saying, “I will surely bless you and multiply your descendants.”

lines.text: God made a promise to Abraham — Abraham is the man God chose to make into a great nation.
To swear is to give your word that a promise is true.
Someone who swears calls on someone greater to back up the promise.
But no one is greater than God.
So God had no one greater than Himself to swear by.
So God swore by Himself.
God Himself backs up His promise to Abraham.
God said to Abraham, “I will surely bless you” — to bless someone is to speak or do good to them.
God also said to Abraham, “I will multiply your descendants.”

passages.scripture: And so Abraham, after waiting patiently, obtained the promise.

lines.text: To wait patiently is to keep trusting God for a long time without giving up.
God had sworn to keep His promise, and so Abraham waited patiently.
And then, after waiting, Abraham obtained the promise God had made to him.
